chapter.title: Chapter One: Block Party
chapter.subtitle: Take the block, keep the receipts.
chapter.description: A neighborhood rivalry turns into a public test of your gang.

tips: Play where district rules help your card.
You only need two districts to win.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, before they've said anything.)* You here for the Block Party Open? Good. Because there's about four people on this block who could win, and three of 'em are related.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I can hear you, Cornball.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Then hear this one asking for a seat. *(To the player.)* I'm Cornball. He's Blue. He thinks the folding tables came with a *government*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: They're municipal. *(Beat.)* And nobody plays till they're on the sheet. Everybody who wants in plays check-in with me first. Beat me, you're on tonight's sheet. That's the process.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: And if I lose?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You're on tonight's sheet.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Beat me or not, I'm on the sheet.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: That's the *spirit* of it. Everybody plays check-in. Somebody's got to see you before I let you near a table.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *Can I say the actual thing?*

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: No.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Win the whole thing and your crew gets a regular place to play. A *regular place*. Not a favour, not a look, not "yeah that'll be alright" — a *line on a sheet with a name on it*. Nobody makes you

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: pick a side to get it. That's the whole flyer. That right there, that's the flyer.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I'm not making anybody pick a side.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Man, you *just* did. You just made a guy beat you *twice* before you let him read a flyer.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What are we playing?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Recovering.)* That. Yes. Shuffle. And for the record, I gave you a chance to just sign the sheet like a normal person.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I'll take the chance.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Two districts takes the match. Dealer goes last.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* All right. You're on the entry sheet.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Look at that. A name he didn't have saved as "cousin."

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Take your deck to my table. *(Beat.)* That was check-in. The qualifier's separate. There's a qualifier.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: There is.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: It's — it's a *thing we do.*

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Cornball said you made me do the same match twice.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: I said no such thing.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: He absolutely did.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: All right. Yeah. I know what I did. You came in here and you were *good*, and I figured if I played you once and beat you, you'd go home and I'd never have to think about it again. That was the

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *whole idea*. That was the idea before I had it.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: *(Off, from a table she is clearly in charge of.)* Blue.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: What.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: You can lose to somebody and let them keep their chair. That's not a rule you have to make up tonight.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: If I'd lost check-in, would I have been able to play at all?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You'd have played the qualifier and hoped.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: You'd have played and hoped, and the qualifier's not the same, and you know it's not the same, and you said you read the flyer *twice* to be ready for tonight.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I read it once.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: You read it *four* times, I printed it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(To the player, low, while Blue is distracted.)*That's the whole tournament, champ. Everybody's got a way they decide who's allowed. Red's is *paperwork*. Blue's is a *rematch*. Same door,

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: different lock.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: What's yours?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Vending machine. *(He nods toward it.)* It's got my three dollars. Don't laugh, that's a *whole situation*.

tips: Cheap cards establish a lead before big finishers arrive.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Same table.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: It's a *regular* tournament. It stays in one place.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Same shuffle.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I shuffle the same way.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Same hand.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You noticed the *hand*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I'm not going to pretend I didn't.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Hold on. Before you play him again. *(To the player, not to Blue.)*Whoever wins tonight picks the open-play nights. That's the actual prize. The Crown, the ceremony, all of it — that's

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *presentation*. That's for the photographs. What the winner actually *gets* is a calendar, and whoever's on the calendar gets to play, and the person who fills that calendar decides who comes to

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I was building up to it.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: You have been building up to it since I unloaded the chairs.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I kept this tournament going four years. I don't hand it to a stranger because they read a flyer.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Then play them. That's what the flyer says.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: So the Crown's a schedule.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: The Crown's a *calendar*. The trophy is a *prop*. *(Beat.)* Don't let anybody tell you different, including me, and especially him.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Very flat.)* The schedule is a *responsibility*.

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: Yes.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: It's a *responsibility*, Wifey, and I have been doing it for four years for *free*, and nobody on this block has ever once — *(He stops. He can hear how that sentence is going.)*

preDialogue.speaker: Wifey
preDialogue.text: *(Not unkind. Worse than unkind.)* Blue. Keep going.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(He doesn't.)* Shuffle.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Quietly, to the table.)* You earned it. Your crew gets the same shot as mine. That's — that's the whole thing. That's what I was protecting.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: I heard that.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: I know you heard it.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: I'm just going to say it back, so we're clear about what happened. He said the right thing *after* he tried to make you lose twice in an hour. I'm not ruining it. I'm just *dating* it.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Consulting a clipboard nobody asked him to be holding.)*Can I say — and I'm being *supportive* here — that this is the fourth conversation tonight where somebody's explained the flyer to Blue,

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: and Blue's a grown man, and at some point the flyer is just gonna have to *fight* for itself.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Cornball, I will bench you.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: You *did* bench me. I'm on the *alley* over there. I've been on the alley since seven.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: He runs the alley. He runs the alley and he's never once said so.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: I run a *lot* of things, Wifey. That's the *shape* of a man.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: If the schedule's the prize — who's the other side? I've only played you.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(A beat too long.)* Red's across the street. He runs a different thing. He does *records*.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: He does *paperwork*, he does *contracts*, he has *four binders*, and he will tell you what you owe him if you *win*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: He signs the entry. You can't get to the roof without Red.

postDialogue.speaker: Wifey
postDialogue.text: You can't get to the roof without *Blue either*, and you *are* Blue, so that sentence is doing a lot of work right now.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Listen. Across the street, he's going to be *polite* to you, and he's going to be *right* about everything, and he's going to run a camera the entire time. Don't let it make you feel small. He's

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: not being mean. That's just how he *holds a thing*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: How do you know him?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I've known him a long time.

tips: The middle district closes in round two—commit elsewhere or wait it out.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Extending a hand.)* I'm Red. Blue said you got lucky. Usually means you played well.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Does he say that a lot?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: He says it when somebody wins. I say it when somebody wins, and then I have to sign their sheet, which is a different kind of sentence. *(Beat.)*Two qualifiers on my side tonight. Win both, I'll

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: sign the entry for the roof.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Off, already filming.)* I'm filming! Give me a name, a rivalry, and one thing you're ashamed of. That's a *format*. I invented it. Nobody's ever escaped it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Give him nothing. He's here to watch cards.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I'm here to *witness*. I'm a *journalist*. There's a *difference* and the difference is the money.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Middle district closes in round two on my side. If you're going to plan for anything, plan for the outside lanes. *(He sets a recorder on the table — an actual recorder, not a phone.)*Camera

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: ready?

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: It's *always* ready. It's a — *(He gestures at himself.)* It's a whole *situation*.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(To the player, mid-match, warmly.)* Okay, honest question, and there's no wrong answer because I'll use either one. What'd you drive here?

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Does it matter?

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: It *always* matters. That's the *content*. I asked a man last month what he was running from and he said a *bus*, and I got eleven minutes of video out of it and it *printed*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Without turning around.)* He said a bus because you offered him four answers and three of them were worse than true.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: They were *options*, Red.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: They were *menus*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Quietly, mid-game, to nobody.)* You can tell what somebody's doing by what they turn the camera toward.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I'm not filming cards, I'm filming the *room*—

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I know. That's the problem. *(Beat.)*There's a man at that table who has been in four of my qualifier videos and I have never once seen his face, and I know the sound of him and I know which chair

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: he sits in, and that is *not* a thing you did on purpose.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat, and for once there's no joke.)* …Okay. Okay, I'll go wide.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: You'll go wide, and then you'll go back to close in about ten minutes, because it's a better shot. But you'll have been *asked*, and that changes what you do with it.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: First one's yours. Come back for the second. *(Beat.)* And I'm going to ask you something as a person, not as the man with the sheet.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Go ahead.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: He said you'd be good because you're good. He didn't say you'd be good so you'd leave. *(Beat — and he holds it, because Red is a man who waits.)*If he had, I'd have said no. That's not a *rule*

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: I've got, it's just what I'd have done.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: You don't have to tell me that.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: I know. I did it anyway. *(Beat.)* That's about half of everything I do.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Reviewing the take, loudly, into the phone.)* Hold on — can you look more devastated? People scroll past a respectful defeat. They *stop* for devastation. It's a *human* thing.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Upload the whole match.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: The *whole* match. You got hit with a big one. That was a big one, Red. That's a *thumbnail*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Flat.)* Upload the whole match.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* …Yeah. Okay. That channel grew *really* fast, though. Just so you know.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: That's the *channel*, not the *record*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: You keep the camera on after you lose?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Every match I ever lose is the one I need.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(To the player, delighted.)* See, that *is* content, that's the *thing*, he *knows* it's the thing, he *wants* you to—

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: He asked me a question and I answered it. That is a *conversation*, Snitch, and you are going to stop putting a *frame* around it.

tips: Save Motion for a contested district.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Not to the player. To Red, from across the table, holding a scorebook.)* Red. Why is my brother's memorial program in your scorebook?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Because I kept it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You kept a *funeral program* in a *scorebook.*

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I kept it in a *binder*, Blue, which is worse, because a binder means it has a *tab*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You kept it for four years.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I've kept it every day since the second of March. That's not a decision I made. I put it in the binder the week I made the binder. *(Beat.)*The binder is for the tournament. The program is in the

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *back*. It was never *in* the scorebook. You just happened to open the scorebook, and I have been waiting four years for somebody to open the scorebook.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: He used to write his scores in it. Before. Cracked. He'd write his scores in the *program* like it was a *scorebook*, in the back, in pen, and then he'd put it back in the drawer and I never told

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: him he was doing it, and then one day he was gone, and it's still got his handwriting in it, and if you throw that binder out I'm going to have to have a *conversation* with you about it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I'm not throwing it out.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I know you're not. I said it so you'd have to *answer* that you weren't. *(Beat.)* You didn't.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: What's the difference.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: The difference is I got to hear you say it while you were angry, and now I know it's *real*, and now I can stop *checking*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Quietly, to the player, so only the player hears it.)* Champion. Come here a second. *(He walks the player to the fence, away from the two of them.)* I got a professional question.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Okay.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: What's a binder *for*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Papers.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah. And what's a *scorebook* for.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Scores.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: And what's a *memorial program* for.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Telling somebody where to sit.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Right. *(Beat.)*Blue, he's got a brother who's been gone four years and he went through that man's *own paperwork* to find out if his brother was coming to *his* tournament. And Red has had that

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *binder* in a *drawer* for four years with a man's *handwriting* in the back of it, and he checks it every *day* so he knows nobody's *touched* it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Cornball.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I'm not *being* anything. I'm *counting.* That's what I do.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I'm going to say something in front of your friend and then I'm never going to say it again, so I'd like you to actually hear it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Say it.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I went looking too. The week it happened. I went to every tournament on this block that had an entry sheet and I checked the *books*, and I found him in *two* of them, and in both of them he was a

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *participant*, not a *winner*, and I took that as a *sign*, and I have been carrying that sign around for four years and it has never once gotten any lighter.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: Red—

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: I'm not asking you for anything. I'm telling you the *number* so you know what I'm carrying. Because you've got a binder and a hundred shirts and a *father* who stood up at a service, and

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: everybody in this block has a *version*, and I want there to be *one* moment in this whole thing where somebody says a *real* number out loud.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Very long beat.)* How many.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Two.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: *(To Red.)* Did either one of them have a name on the list for a person bringing them?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* No.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Was there a "+1" or a partner line?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: No.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Then you were looking for a man who plays alone, and you found two men who were *with somebody*, and you kept going.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Long silence.)* …I kept going.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Then it's not a sign. It's a Tuesday. People bring people.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Putting the binder down, which he has not done once all night.)* That is an extremely cheap thing to say to a man who hasn't slept.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: I know. It's still true.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: That's two. Your entry's signed.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Still standing there, binder under his arm.)* You're not gonna say anything else about that?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: I'm gonna say one thing. *(Beat.)* You asked me why I kept it, and I gave you a *reason*, and the reason is real, and it's not the *reason*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: What's the reason?

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*I kept it because it was the last thing he touched, and because if I'd put it in a *file* I would have had to *look* at it, and I did not want to *look* at it, and I have not looked at it

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: in four years, and I am *telling you that out loud* so it stops being something I can do.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Red—

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Don't. *(He picks the binder up.)* Go play your qualifier. Take your friend. *(To the player.)* Cross the street, the roof's through the alley.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(To nobody.)* …That was *filmed*, by the way. I didn't get to ask first, and I want it noted that I *could have*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: You did not ask first. He did not ask either. You are *all* learning the same lesson tonight.

tips: This mastery fade is optional and never blocks the main route.

starObjectives.description: Move at least one of your cards.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Not a greeting. A pitch.)* Rooftop route's straight ahead. Or you stop here and play me for a cardback tag. Winners get a tag. It's a real tag. It's *physical*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What do I get if I lose?

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: You keep walking.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: That's not a prize.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: That's a *loss*, champ, and I said what it was. *(Beat.)*You want me to pretend there's something on the other side so you'll take the match? I don't *need* you to take the match. I've got nine

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: people on this card and one of them is my aunt.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Before we do *any* of that, I need to address an *injustice*.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: I know. Nine dollars, right?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: **Three.**

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: What.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *Three dollars.* It was three dollars. It was a dollar and it took a dollar and it gave me a *hot water*, and I have been *carrying* that — — I have been carrying this since **August**, and I want

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: the *alley* to know that I am not *performing* a complaint, I am *submitting* one.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Looking at the slip.)* That's a *receipt*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: It is a *receipt* and it is *dated* and it is the *only* evidence I have that anybody in this city has ever *owed* me anything under two hundred dollars.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: The machine's over there. It's the one that takes 'em.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: I *know* it's the one. I have a *relationship* with that machine. I have *named* that machine. *(Beat.)* Her name is Dell.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Is it broken?

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: It's *operational*. It's *operational* in the way a person is operational.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: She's *fine*. She's *been* fine. What she's not is *fair*, and I've written to the *company*, and I have written to the *company* *four times*, and I have never once received a response from a

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *human*, and I have started to take that personally.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What did she give you?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Hot water.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Hot water?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: **Unsweetened sparkling water.** In a *bottle*. Hot. *(Beat.)*It was *hot* and it was *flat* and it cost me *two dollars*, and I have been drinking it *carefully*, one *sip* at a time, for six

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: weeks, because when it's gone it's gone and I have *nothing*, champ.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Genuinely sympathetic.)* That's a hard position.

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: Thank you. It *is* a hard position.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Why not just put it in the fridge?

preDialogue.speaker: Cornball
preDialogue.text: *(Offended.)* To *whose* fridge?

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: I'm Alley Runner. I deliver things, and I move cards when people stop watching the other districts. *(Beat.)* Which is every district, all the time, but I'm not gonna be bitter about it.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You move cards *during* a tournament?

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: I *watch* a tournament. Sometimes I'm also walking through it. Those are two different activities and I'm good at both, and the second one pays better.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Is that cheating?

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* That is a *great* question and I want to be honest with you, because everyone in this city has a version of me they're sure of, and I'd rather you got the real one from me.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: I don't touch anybody's cards. I move *mine*. I deliver things for people who can't leave their tables, and I go through a venue on a route that has nothing to do with the tournament, and if a man

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: is losing in a spot where the wind is bad, I'll be standing in the wind, and he'll have a card he didn't have an hour ago, and he'll be *mad* at a shuffle, and he'll *keep* the card, and he'll

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: never know it was me.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: And if that changes the match?

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: Then it changed the *feel* of the match, and the *feel* of the match is what a man remembers four years later. *(Beat.)*I'm not here to cheat anybody. I'm here to make sure the *alley* wins,

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: because the alley never gets a qualifier, never gets a table, and never gets *noticed*, and I have got a *system*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: That's fair.

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Surprised.)* Huh. People usually ask what my *rate* is.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Is there a rate?

preDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
preDialogue.text: *(Grudging respect.)* There is a rate. It's for *other people*. I don't charge people I like. *(Beat.)* I like you. Go beat the man with the microphone.

postDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
postDialogue.text: Nice catch. Tag's yours.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(To nobody, narrating.)* And here we are. The *moment*. *(Beat.)* Please be the one.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: It's cold.

postDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
postDialogue.text: It's cold.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: It's *cold* and it's *flat* and it cost me *three dollars over six weeks* and — *(He turns the bottle around. Reads the label.)* It's *sparkling water*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Is that bad?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)*It's *cold*, champ. *(Beat.)*It's *cold* and it's *flat* and it is *mine*, and I have been *arguing with a machine* since August, and I have *won*, and I would like the *alley* to

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: acknowledge that I have won, because there is *nobody else* who would.

postDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
postDialogue.text: *(Handing him a second bottle, from under his own table, unprompted.)* Here.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: Where'd that come from?

postDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
postDialogue.text: I've got a *cooler*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: You've had a *cooler* this whole time?

postDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
postDialogue.text: I've had a cooler all *night*, Cornball. I run a *business*. I *just* don't talk about it, because you would have *asked*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Holding two bottles, both cold, both flat, both free.)* *(Beat.)* Would I have.

postDialogue.speaker: Alley Runner
postDialogue.text: You would have asked me *twice*, and then you would have told the *block*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: I been *bribed*, champ. A man slipped me a *free water* to keep me from *questioning* him. That's *corruption*. I'm a *compromised* man. Somebody write that down.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Somebody?

postDialogue.speaker: Cornball
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* …Yeah. That's a whole thing I'll think about later.

starObjectives.description: Move at least one of your cards.

tips: Snitch's Watching the Feed gives a deterministic CPU Motion bump in round four.

phases.name: Watching the Feed
phases.description: At round four, Snitch cashes the camera chatter into +2 CPU Motion.

passive.name: Watching the Feed
passive.description: At round four, Snitch cashes the camera chatter into +2 Motion.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: There you are. Last qualifier before the roof. *(Beat.)* Winner meets tonight's special guest.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Already there.)* Who's the guest.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Paid entrance.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *How much.*

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Very fast.)* I said *paid entrance*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: How much did you *take*.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I said I *can't say*, and what I *did* say is that he was *very specific* about the *arrival time*, which is more than most clients are, and he sent a *note*, and the note said

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Snitch checks a folded paper)*— it said, and I'm reading it *exactly* as written, "the champion gets a *reason* to be on the roof, so don't let him be modest about it."

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Somebody briefed you.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Somebody briefed me *beautifully*. I had a *whole run of bit* planned and they ruined it by being *specific*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Private clients don't usually rent a smoke machine.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: This one did. I'm not even going to *pretend* I didn't read into that. *(Beat.)*There's a *whole stranger* on my roof tonight and I've been told *nothing*, and I have *feelings* about that, and

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: I've decided to have them *loudly*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: What did the note promise you?

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Huh.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: You said he sent a note. Notes to people like you are usually about *them*.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Slowly, like he's been caught out.)*He said I'd get the *clip*. Not the money — I'd get the *clip*. Of the *final*, tonight, *first*, before anybody posts, and he said it like a thing that

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *mattered* to him, which — *(Beat.)*which it *didn't*, because the final's between two people and neither of 'em *knows he's up there*, so what would he *do* with a clip?

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Then he's not here to watch you.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: Oh, that's — *(He puts the phone down.)* Oh, he's not here for *me*. He's got *a match to win* and he needed somebody to *put a roof under him* so the *entrance* looked like it was a *thing*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: *(Quietly.)* He's four years late. He's allowed an entrance.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(Horrified.)* I have been *working for the villain*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: He gets a boost in round four. Don't spend everything, because he will not stop talking.

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: That's *defamatory*—

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: It's *records*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Round four. How do you know it works?

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: Because I wrote the rules. *(Beat.)* I write everybody's rules. Blue thinks he runs his because he *shouts*, and I run mine because I *mail them*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: That's a strange way to run a tournament.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: It's a strange way to run a *family*. *(Beat.)* We do the same thing.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: You win. Go up. Your opponent's already there.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: You booked somebody and didn't show me the name.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: I *told* you the name. You didn't *listen*.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: I listened to *paid entrance*. I did not hear a *name*.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Folding the note, and folding it wrong, twice.)* He said "they said you knew them."

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat. A long one.)* …Which did he say. *They.*

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: I didn't — I wasn't *checking*—

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* …Mm.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: Red—

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(Not turning round. He picks up the sheet.)* Say it again tonight and I'll have it in a *document*, Snitch, and neither of us wants that. *(Beat.)* Go up.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: …Right.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(To the player, and it costs him something to be calm.)* Go up.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Red—

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: Go up, and play, and I'll be up there in a minute, and whatever happens up there I need you to have *played your part* first. *(Beat.)*Because if I go up there before you've finished, this is

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: going to be about me.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: It's already about you.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
postDialogue.text: *(And he almost smiles, which is worse.)* I know. I just wanted one room to be about you first.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(To the player, at the stairs.)* Kid. For what it's worth — I've been doing this eight years and I've never seen anybody *not* text that man. Not once. Whoever he is, he *knew* about the phone.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: Thanks.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: Don't thank me, I *hired* him.

passive.name: Three Deep
passive.description: Cracked Head escalates through three one-time phases as the block changes hands.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Not to anyone. To the table.)* No.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: No, what the *fuck* is this.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: It's me, Blue.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: We had a *service*. I paid to put your face on a hundred shirts.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: A *hundred*, Red. A *hundred*. I stood outside a *hardware store* for an *hour* and a man in a *jacket* said that was a *lot* of shirts for a community, and I said it's *his* community, and the

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: man said *all right*, and I went back to work on *Tuesday*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: And what did I want? I didn't want them *gone*. *(Beat.)* I wanted somebody to *say his name*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: I wanted one person in this *city* to say "I wonder what happened to Cracked Head" in a *normal voice* at a *normal thing*, and I would have paid for that, and I would have paid for it with a

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *hundred shirts*, and I would have been *delighted* — and nobody *ever* said it. Not *once*. Four *years*. Not a *soul*.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: I know.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: You *know*? You *know* what I did with four years? I have been *raising* you. I have been *keeping* you. There's a *binder* on this island with your handwriting in the *back* of it, because Red

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *never once* threw it out, and I have to sit across from that man at a *card table* every Tuesday and pretend he's not *holding my brother* in a *drawer*.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Red
preDialogue.text: "Snitch. Put the phone down."

preDialogue.speaker: Snitch
preDialogue.text: *(To nobody, very quietly.)* I am going to *lose my job*.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: *(Not loud. Not brave. Just — out.)* I think somebody's going to want the chairs moved.

preDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
preDialogue.text: *(Not turning.)* What.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: My table's blocking the door. And if this is what it is, I don't want *my* chair to be the first thing somebody sees when they come in.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Move the chairs.

preDialogue.speaker: Player
preDialogue.text: Yeah.

preDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
preDialogue.text: Yeah. *(Beat.)* Good. Move them.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: You won. Clean. I'm not taking that from you.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: So you can say three honest words to a *stranger*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Good game.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: That's *two*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* I'm tired.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You're *tired*. Four *years*, and that's what you —

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Blue.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You get to be tired *after*. You don't get to be tired *first*. That's the whole — *(He stops, because he can hear it.)*That's the whole thing you've been doing for *four years*, and you're still

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: doing it, right now, on a *roof*, in front of *Snitch*.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* You're going to do that for a while.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Yeah.

postDialogue.speaker: Cracked Head
postDialogue.text: Okay. Do it for a while. I'm not in a *rush*. *(Beat.)* I've got nowhere to be tonight.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: *(Not to either of them. To the room.)*There's a vending machine downstairs that eats your money and there's a man who's been drinking flat water for six weeks because of it. Could use somebody

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: else bringing something up. *(Beat.)*Not a *thing*. Just, somebody's got to.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(Already moving.)* I have got a *cooler*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: I know you have. I heard you.

postDialogue.speaker: Snitch
postDialogue.text: *(At the stairs, delighted and doomed.)* I have got a *cooler* and *no friends*, and that is the *most* me thing that has ever happened to a man.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: You didn't have to move the chairs.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: They were blocking the door.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: Everybody in this city has an opinion about my brother and you're the only one that did *something*.

postDialogue.speaker: Player
postDialogue.text: It was a chair.

postDialogue.speaker: Ganger Blue
postDialogue.text: *(Beat.)* Yeah. It was.

tips: Chapter Two is unlocked after this ceremony.
10 Street Pack tickets is one upgraded ten-pull at the gym.
Use your 250 Clout training fund at the Trading Post: Practice Session adds character XP; Move Coaching unlocks Corner Advice at level 2.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: Congratulations. Your crew has a home table now. Pick the nights — I'll help you get everybody on the schedule.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: So the crown's the schedule.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: The crown's the *permission*. The schedule's the *thing you do with it*. Nobody tells you that. Everybody thinks you win a *thing*. You win a *duty*, and if you don't do it, then you just took a

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *duty* off a man who was *already drowning* in it.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: Please put me down somewhere far from the vending machine.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: The machine's not here.

scenes.speaker: Cornball
scenes.text: I don't care. I got a *problem* with that machine and I need to be *at least a county* away from it on principle.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Move. I need to see him.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: I was going to come by.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: My house. Remember that place? *(Beat.)* I've been at the *same address* since before your memorial, and there's a *man* living in it now, and he introduced himself to me by name.

scenes.speaker: Cracked Head
scenes.text: Can we talk alone?

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: After making your entrance in front of the *whole block*? Now you want *alone*?

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: There's a message you need to hear. He sent it to me after he left.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: After he left. You mean after we *buried him in our heads*.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Yes.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* How long was the message.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: Four words.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Where is it.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: I'm not carrying it around.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Then who is.

scenes.speaker: Ganger Red
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* I am.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: *(To Wifey, quietly.)* Should I pick it up.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* If you don't, Blue will. And if Blue picks it up right now, in front of all of them, with his brother standing eight feet away, then the next four years of this block are about *that*.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: Picks up the crown. Puts it on. It is a plastic tiara and it does not fit and nobody laughs, which is the joke.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Almost.)* There. Now it's *yours* and now we can have the *actual* thing.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: You're the one that won it.

scenes.speaker: Player
scenes.text: Yes ma'am.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Then you hold the *paper*. When this is over, everybody's going to want to *tell you things* about him, and some of 'em are going to be *true*, and you're going to want to be *polite* about it.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Beat.)*Don't. There's gonna be one person in this room who tells you something and it will be about *four years* and it will be about *you*, and you hold the *paper* and you say "I'll get back

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: to you."

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: Get the recorder. Nobody is disappearing before I hear it.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(Not to anybody. To the room, the way she has talked since 1998.)* There's a chair at that table when he comes.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(Not looking up from the sheet.)* I'll put it in.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: I didn't say a *chair*, Wifey. *(Beat.)*I said there's a *chair*. I meant I'd built one. *(Beat — and she does not look at Baby Momma, and that is why it lands.)*I need a seat at that table where

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: the *baby's people* are, and I'm not being romantic, I'm being *practical*. I've watched this family hold every funeral and every meeting in the same six chairs, and the baby's people have been

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *standing* in this *kitchen* for four years, and I am *done* with it.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Not turning round. It is a long beat.)*Auntie, he's not coming to a *table* to be *seated*. He's coming to a table to be told what *time breakfast is*, and that's a *different thing*, and it's

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: going to take a *year*.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: Then I'll build the chair anyway. It'll be there when you're ready to hate it.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* Make it a *stool*. He'll never sit in anything with an *arm* on it. Make it a *stool*, and put it by the *door*, and don't let anybody *move* it.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(Beat.)* By the door.

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: By the door. *(Beat.)*And Auntie — — when he comes, and he *will* come, and it *will* be at some *awful* hour of the *morning* — you're not *serving*. You're not *feeding* him. He's not a *guest*

scenes.speaker: Baby Momma
scenes.text: and he's not *company* and he's not *family* yet. You sit down and you *eat* and you let the room be *ordinary*, and that's the *whole* thing, that's the *job*.

scenes.speaker: Church Auntie
scenes.text: *(A beat. And the smallest smile anybody has on this roof.)* I have been doing that since *1998*, baby. I have been *waiting* for somebody to ask.

scenes.speaker: Wifey
scenes.text: *(To the player, and she puts a hand on the table and does not move it.)* Stay a minute, champ. I don't think this celebration's over.
